The write succeeded with no lint hook error this time, meaning the manifest now passes `ent ci --lint` with zero blocking errors.

## Summary

I decomposed `spf13/cobra` (a Go CLI framework) into 6 Logical Units in `/out/manifest.json`:

- **command-core** (domain) — the `Command` type, tree navigation, and execution lifecycle (`command.go`, `command_notwin.go`, `command_win.go`, `cobra.go`)
- **args-validators** (domain) — pluggable positional-argument rules (`args.go`)
- **flag-groups** (domain) — required-together/one-required/mutually-exclusive flag constraints (`flag_groups.go`)
- **completion-engine** (domain) — the runtime `__complete` logic and ActiveHelp (`completions.go`, `active_help.go`)
- **shell-completion-scripts** (infra) — generates/writes bash/zsh/fish/powershell completion scripts (`bash_completions*.go`, `zsh_completions.go`, `fish_completions.go`, `powershell_completions.go`, `shell_completions.go`)
- **doc-generators** (domain) — man/Markdown/reST/YAML doc generation, separate `doc` package (`doc/*.go`)

All 19 non-test `.go` files are partitioned; tests, docs, CI, and tooling are listed under `excluded`. The `violations_observed` section documents 7 real internal-reach couplings the scouts found (e.g., `args.go` calling unexported `command.go` helpers, a two-way dependency between completion-engine and shell-completion-scripts) rather than papering over them.
